lessons.name: The gate equals its intent: accept(signed, verifies) = (signed ∧ verifies) at every state — the multiplication IS the boolean AND, proven.
lessons.why: The gate equals its intent: accept(signed, verifies) = (signed ∧ verifies) at every state — the multiplication IS the boolean AND, proven.

lessons.name: The authentication gate as a truth table: accept(signed, verifies) = signed·verifies over {0,1}² is 1 only when BOTH hold — a command is accepted exactly when it is signed and its tag verifies.
lessons.why: The authentication gate as a truth table: accept(signed, verifies) = signed·verifies over {0,1}² is 1 only when BOTH hold — a command is accepted exactly when it is signed and its tag verifies.

lessons.name: A failing or tampered tag is rejected: when the tag does not verify (verifies = 0), accept(s, 0) = 0 even if the command is signed — a wrong or altered signature does not pass.
lessons.why: A failing or tampered tag is rejected: when the tag does not verify (verifies = 0), accept(s, 0) = 0 even if the command is signed — a wrong or altered signature does not pass.

lessons.name: Exactly ONE presented tag verifies — the correct one (here the expected value 5). Of all 8 candidate tags, only the matching MAC passes; every forgery or tampered tag fails. The gate is precise.
lessons.why: Exactly ONE presented tag verifies — the correct one (here the expected value 5). Of all 8 candidate tags, only the matching MAC passes; every forgery or tampered tag fails. The gate is precise.

lessons.name: An unsigned command is never accepted: with no tag (signed = 0), accept(0, v) = 0 whatever the verify bit — no signature, no entry.
lessons.why: An unsigned command is never accepted: with no tag (signed = 0), accept(0, v) = 0 whatever the verify bit — no signature, no entry.

lessons.name: Tampering the message changes the tag: for an injective keyed tag mac(k,m) = (7 + m) mod 9, distinct messages carry distinct tags — so an altered message no longer matches the old signature. The accept gate still fires only on signed∧verifies (accept 1 1 = 1). (A model of the property; the real MAC is HMAC-SHA256.)
lessons.why: Tampering the message changes the tag: for an injective keyed tag mac(k,m) = (7 + m) mod 9, distinct messages carry distinct tags — so an altered message no longer matches the old signature. The accept gate still fires only on signed∧verifies (accept 1 1 = 1). (A model of the property; the real MAC is HMAC-SHA256.)

lessons.name: Why the MAC must be HMAC-SHA256— (k⊕m₁) ⊕ (m₁⊕m₂) = k⊕m₂, so seeing one command's tag lets an attacker forge another. Authentication demands a NONLINEAR keyed MAC (HMAC-SHA256, KAT-verified); this is the honest reason the toy tag is refused.
